claims: The UConn Huskies men's basketball program has won six NCAA Division I National Championships in 1999, 2004, 2011, 2014, 2023, and 2024.
The UConn Huskies men's basketball program is tied for third all-time in NCAA Division I National Championships.
The UConn Huskies men's basketball program won back-to-back NCAA Division I National Championships in 2023 and 2024 under coach Dan Hurley.
In 1999, UConn men's basketball defeated Duke 77–74 in the NCAA Division I National Championship game under coach Jim Calhoun.
In 2004, UConn men's basketball defeated Georgia Tech 82–73 in the NCAA Division I National Championship game under coach Jim Calhoun.
In 2011, UConn men's basketball defeated Butler 53–41 in the NCAA Division I National Championship game under coach Jim Calhoun.
In 2014, UConn men's basketball defeated Kentucky 60–54 in the NCAA Division I National Championship game under coach Kevin Ollie.
In 2023, UConn men's basketball defeated San Diego State 76–59 in the NCAA Division I National Championship game under coach Dan Hurley.
In 2024, UConn men's basketball defeated Purdue 75–60 in the NCAA Division I National Championship game under coach Dan Hurley.
Prior to their 2026 runner-up finish, UConn men's basketball was 6-0 in national championship games.
UConn men's basketball finished runner-up in 2026.
Since 1999, UConn men's basketball has won six NCAA Division I National Championships, the most of any school in that span.
In 2024, UConn men's basketball became the eighth school in NCAA Division I history to win consecutive titles.
Jim Calhoun has led the UConn Huskies men's basketball to 3 NCAA Division I National Championships.
Kevin Ollie has led the UConn Huskies men's basketball to 1 NCAA Division I National Championship.
Dan Hurley has led the UConn Huskies men's basketball to 2 NCAA Division I National Championships.
The University of Connecticut women’s basketball team is a separate program from the UConn Huskies men's basketball program.
The University of Connecticut women’s basketball team has 11 NCAA Division I championships.
